one_month_reasoning: The window to 2026-11-01 very likely contains Avnet's fiscal Q1 FY27 report (quarter ends Oct 3; last year's Q1 was reported Oct 29, so expect ~Oct 28-29, 2026). Guidance is sales $9.0-9.3B and adj EPS $2.80-2.90. In an upcycle with ~10% sequential growth guided, a beat is likely, but the stock is up ~105% in a year, sits near its 52-week high and above the average sell-side target ($106), so a beat is largely expected; the swing factor is the Q2 guide and commentary on memory pricing (about a third of recent growth), double ordering and cash burn (management flagged more working-capital outflow in Q1). I see no clear directional edge, so I use a roughly symmetric lognormal centred on today's price with sigma ~12% (above the 10.6% monthly norm of 37%/3.5 because of the earnings event), shaded very slightly lower at the money for post-run reversal and cash-flow headline risk.

fair_value.method: Blend of NTM P/E ($11.50 x 9x = $103.5, 40%), normalized through-cycle EPS ($7.60 x 12x = $91, 40%) and price/book on projected Sep-2027 book ($68/sh x 1.6x = $109, 20%) gives ~$100, slightly below the $106.94 price because peak-cycle earnings are capitalised at above-history multiples.

inputs_detail.input: NTM EPS as of Oct 2027 (roughly FY28 first half + FY27 second half)
inputs_detail.derivation: Q1 guide x4 = $11.40 run-rate; consensus FY27 $10.57 looks stale vs that run-rate, but ~1/3 of growth is memory price inflation that should fade (source 2), so I hold NTM EPS near the run-rate rather than extrapolating sequential growth.

At the last earnings peak (FY23 adj EPS $8.06, source 6) distributors traded at mid-single-digit P/Es; I allow a premium (9x vs ~6-7x) for the stronger margin structure and AI/memory-shortage duration, while bearish sell-side (Wells Fargo Sell, $80 target, source 4/9) argues for less.
Simple average of trough ($3.44), prior peak ($8.06) and current run-rate ($11.40).
Mid-cycle multiple for a low-margin, working-capital-heavy distributor; slightly above typical 10-11x to credit improved EC margins (4.1%) and Farnell recovery (9.0%).
$5,022M/84M = ~$60/sh today plus ~$11 adj EPS less ~$1.5 dividends and GAAP-adjustments/charges (FY26 GAAP EPS $4.01 vs adj $5.67) -> ~+$8.
Distributor ROE at peak ~16-18% (adj EPS ~$11 on ~$64 avg book) supports 1.4-1.8x; midpoint used.

bear.story: Memory price inflation (~1/3 of recent growth) peaks in 2027, customers who built safety stock/double-ordered digest inventory, sequential sales roll over in H2 FY27; cash burn plus 3x+ gross leverage and a negative Fitch outlook keep buybacks off; market re-rates to prior-peak ~6.5x on falling ~$9.5 NTM EPS.

base.story: Upcycle continues but decelerates; NTM EPS ~$11.5, multiple slips modestly to ~9x as investors look through to peak; leverage falls toward 3.0x and buybacks resume; stock roughly flat from here.

bull.story: Memory/AI-driven shortage lasts into 2028, mass-market and Western industrial demand recover broadly, EC margins move toward 4.5-5%; EPS run-rate $13-14 at ~10.5x.

thesis_break_reason: ~33% below today and ~6.3x run-rate EPS, i.e. back to prior-peak multiples; trading there would most likely mean the market has evidence the cycle has turned (sequential sales decline or guide-down, memory price reversal, an inventory/double-order unwind) or a credit event (rating downgrade, covenant pressure from working-capital debt build), not ordinary 37%-vol noise.

catalysts.event: Q1 FY27 results and Q2 guide (expected late Oct; guide $9.0-9.3B sales, $2.80-2.90 EPS)
Q2 FY27 results: first read on whether sequential growth slows as memory pricing laps
Q3 FY27 results; lead-time and backlog commentary (double-ordering tell)
Q4 FY27 results and FY28 framing; buyback resumption once gross leverage ~3.0x
Memory contract pricing trend (DRAM/NAND) and supply additions
Rating agency actions (Fitch negative outlook) and convertible-note dilution above $70.27 conversion price

key_uncertainties: How long the memory shortage and price inflation last (trade sources say into 2028) vs a 2027 peak
Extent of customer safety-stock building/double ordering hidden in backlog
Working-capital cash burn (FY26 OCF -$281M) and leverage (gross ~3.2x) limiting buybacks and inviting rating pressure
Peak-cycle multiple: market currently pays ~9.4x run-rate EPS vs mid-single digits at the FY23 peak
reasoning: Facts: FY26 sales $27.6B (+25%), Q4 sales $8.3B (+48% y/y), Q4 adj EPS $2.28, Q1 FY27 guide $9.15B / $2.85 (run-rate ~$11.40). Skeptic findings: (1) roughly a third of Q4 sequential and y/y sales and gross-profit growth came from memory price inflation passed through without markup, and management concedes future increases won't match memory's; (2) management itself flags customer safety-stock building and double-ordering risk, the classic precursor of distributor downturns; (3) FY26 operating cash flow was -$281M (Q4 about -$291M) as receivables rose $2.6B, with more burn flagged for Q1; debt ~$3.2B vs $155M cash, Fitch moved the outlook to negative at 3.7x leverage, and gross leverage is still 3.2x vs a 3.0x target; (4) the 1.75% 2030 converts ($650M, conversion ~$70.27, no capped call disclosed) are in the money, ~3M-share net dilution at today's price; (5) insiders (CEO in May at ~$83, an SVP in August) have been sellers, no buys; (6) Wells Fargo stays Sell ($80) and the average target ($106) is at the price, with 1 Hold, 1 Sell among 4. Weighed honestly: the upturn is real and broad (all regions, Farnell margin 9%), memory tightness may persist into 2028, and EPS is compounding fast, so a short-term collapse is not my base case. Historically distributors trade at mid-single-digit P/Es at peaks (FY23 adj EPS $8.06), so the main downside mechanism is multiple compression as the market anticipates the peak, not an accounting problem; I found no short-seller report, litigation or accounting red flag. Fair value ~$100 (blend of 9x NTM, 12x normalized, 1.6x book). Scenarios 25/50/25 at $62/$105/$145 give a mean ~$104 and median ~$100; the ladder is a right-skewed distribution with ~40% effective vol (above the 37% realized, for cycle-turn risk), median just under the current price. Research was limited to ~15 queries/fetches; the Q4 call transcript and fresh September 2026 news were not fully reachable.
